title: The Event Horizon
objective: After this level you can explain the event horizon and what the first black hole image showed.
summary: The event horizon is the point of no return. In 2019 an Earth-sized network of radio dishes imaged M87’s black hole.

cards.headline: In 2019, humanity saw a black hole for the first time. Sort of.
The point of no return
cards.body: Every black hole is surrounded by an event horizon: the boundary beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape. Outside it, light and matter can still get away. Inside it, there is no way back.

cards.headline: An Earth-sized telescope
cards.body: To see something that small and far away, astronomers linked radio telescopes around the world into the Event Horizon Telescope, which works like one Earth-sized dish. In 2019 it released the first image of a black hole: a dark shadow ringed by glowing gas, at the center of the galaxy M87.

cards.fact: M87’s black hole is about 6.5 billion times the mass of the Sun.
cards.context: It isn’t a stellar black hole but a supermassive one, sitting at the heart of a giant galaxy.

cards.headline: Event horizon: seen
learned: The event horizon is the point of no return
The EHT links dishes into an Earth-sized telescope
It imaged M87’s black hole in 2019
That black hole is ~6.5 billion Suns

questions.prompt: What is a black hole’s event horizon?

options.label: The glowing ring of gas around it
options.rationale: That gas is outside the horizon.

options.label: The boundary beyond which nothing can escape
The center where all its mass sits
options.rationale: The horizon is a boundary, not the center.

options.label: The jet of particles it shoots out
options.rationale: Jets come from outside the horizon.

questions.explanation: The event horizon is the point of no return: beyond it, nothing can escape, not even light.

questions.prompt: Why did the Event Horizon Telescope link dishes all around the world?

options.label: To see the black hole from every side
options.rationale: Earth-sized spacing is about detail, not viewing angle.

options.label: To shield the telescopes from sunlight
To act like one Earth-sized telescope that sees fine detail

questions.explanation: Linked dishes spread across Earth work like one enormous telescope, sharp enough to image a black hole’s shadow.

questions.prompt: From Level 35: the Event Horizon Telescope is a supersized version of which radio-astronomy technique?

options.label: Observing only at night
options.rationale: Radio telescopes can observe by day.

options.label: Cooling the air above the dishes

questions.explanation: Like the arrays in Level 35, the EHT links many dishes, spread across a whole planet.
